The '''Lumablast Rocket''', or '''luma blast''', was a type of [[Wrist rocket/Legends|wrist rocket]] produced by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]] that was designed to temporarily blind [[Species/Legends|living creatures]] with a bright flash of light rather than cause lasting physical harm. The [[Missile/Legends|rockets]] were utilized in the [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher/Legends|MM9 rocket system]], a [[wrist rocket launcher]] produced by [[Kelvarek Consolidated Arms/Legends|Kelvarek Consolidated Arms]]. In [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultist]] [[Granta Omega]] used at least one of the rockets while fighting the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] used Lumablast Rockets in [[Gender/Legends|his]] MM9 rocket system at some point during his career. The effect of a Lumablast Rocket was similar, although less intense, than that of a [[luma grenade]].

==Description==
A type of [[Wrist rocket/Legends|wrist rocket]], the Lumablast Rocket,<ref name="AEG" /> also known simply as a luma blast, was designed to detonate in a bright flash<ref name="W&T">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> of orange and yellow-[[Color/Legends|colored]] light. The flash produced by a Lumablast Rocket was bright enough to still be effective against a member of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with closed [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. A Human could take as long as several [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] to recover after being exposed to a luma blast. While the weapon did not cause any lasting physical damage, the flash of light produced by a Lumablast [[Missile/Legends|Rocket]] was capable of temporarily blinding [[Species/Legends|living creatures]] caught within its four-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] blast radius.<ref name="AEG" /> The rockets had a maximum range of 100 meters<ref name="AEGrange" /> and made a hissing sound when launched.<ref name="JQTFS" /> The flash from a Lumablast Rocket was similar, although not as powerful, as the blast from a [[luma grenade]], which could blind a Human for thirty minutes or up to an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] if the individual was wearing [[Night-vision goggles/Legends|night vision goggles]].<ref name="JQTMOD">''[[Jedi Quest: The Master of Disguise]]''</ref>

==History==
The Lumablast Rocket was produced by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]]<ref name="AEG" /> by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]]<ref name="JQTFS" /><ref name="TERC" /> and was available around the same time as the luma [[grenade]], which was available as early as [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]].<ref name="JQTMOD" /><ref name="TERC" /> The rockets were used in the [[Kelvarek Consolidated Arms/Legends|Kelvarek Consolidated Arms]] [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher/Legends|MM9 rocket system]], a model of [[wrist rocket launcher]]. While that system was being produced, the sale and ownership of Lumablast Rockets was restricted to those with government license and approval, although they were still commonly sold for 400 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] each.<ref name="AEG" /> In 23 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="TERC" /> the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultist]]<ref name="Granta">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030612omega|text=Granta Omega: An Expanded Universe Character}}</ref> [[Granta Omega]] carried at least one of the rockets for use in the wrist rocket launchers [[Gender/Legends|he]] wore while on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. While in Korriban's [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]], Omega used a Lumablast Rocket to temporarily blind the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], but he was ultimately unable to defeat the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] with his other weaponry and was [[Death/Legends|killed]].<ref name="JQTFS" /> The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] utilized Lumablast Rockets in his MM9 rocket system at some point during his career,<ref name="W&T" /> which began during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and continued into the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] over six [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] later.<ref name="FettDate">[[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett's]] career as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] spans from at least [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], according to the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Bounty (episode)|Bounty]]," to at least [[44 ABY]], according to ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]'' and ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Luma blasts were first mentioned in a list of specialty rockets used by Boba Fett that was featured in ''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]'', a [[1997]] reference book written by [[Bill Smith]].<ref name="W&T" /> The rocket was later identified as a Lumablast Rocket in a side bar on ammunition used with the MM9 rocket system in ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]'', a [[2002]] sourcebook written by [[Jeff Grubb]] and [[Owen K.C. Stephens]] for the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook|revised edition]] of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''. In [[2004]], at least one Lumablast Rocket appeared in a fight between Granta Omega and Obi-Wan Kenobi in ''[[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown]]'', a novel written by [[Jude Watson]]. Other wrist rockets were fired during the same scene, but none of them were identified as Lumablast Rockets. The novel also did not identify the type of wrist rocket launcher that Omega used to fire the Lumablast Rocket.<ref name="JQTFS" />

''Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown'' stated that it would take several minutes to recover from the effects of the rocket,<ref name="JQTFS" /> which contradicted information in ''Arms & Equipment Guide'' stating that recovery would take less than a minute. As the sourcebook only provided the recovery time as game mechanics<ref name="AEG" /> and the novel was released afterward, this article uses the novel's recovery time of a several minutes.<ref name="JQTFS" /> In ''Arms and Equipment Guide'', the only era when the Lumablast Rockets were confirmed to be available was the [[Rise of the Empire era]], which is the only era provided for the MM9 rocket system in the book.<ref name="AEG" /> However, while the rockets were not featured with Boba Fett elsewhere, Fett did carry the MM9 rocket system during the Rise of the Empire era, [[Rebellion era]], [[New Republic era]], [[New Jedi Order era]], and [[Legacy era]].<ref name="MM9">Based on the appearance of the [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher/Legends|MM9 rocket system]] in ''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]'', the MM9 rocket system is shown in [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett's]] possession on the cover of ''[[Boba Fett: Pursuit]]'', in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], in ''[[Boba Fett: Murder Most Foul]]'', in "[[Revenants]]," and on the back cover of ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''. These sources occur during the [[Rise of the Empire era]], [[Rebellion era]], [[New Republic era]], [[New Jedi Order era]], and [[Legacy era]], respectively.</ref> While the [[2008]] novel ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]'' revealed that the effects of a luma grenade could be negated using polarized lenses,<ref name="CNJT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> no source has stated that the same was true for Lumablast Rockets.
